title: Dynamical phase transitions for single particles in the semiclassical and weak noise limits
authors: Norayr Asriyan, Jan Meibohm, Vasco Cavina, Massimiliano Esposito
abstract: We present a unifying description of dynamical phase transitions in the unitary evolution of an isolated quantum particle and the dissipative relaxation of a classical Brownian particle, based on a dynamical generat- ing function. In the semiclassical and weak-noise limits, Fisher zeros of this function condense in the complex- time plane and reach the corresponding physical axes, producing dynamical phase transitions through a competition between return trajectories. This establishes a direct connection between quantum and classical (finite-time) dynamical phase transitions, where the semiclassical limit plays the role of the thermodynamic limit. In particular, the established link naturally provides a classical version of the Loschmidt amplitude and shows how dynamical quantum phase transitions, typically associated with isolated many-body systems, can arise in a single-particle quantum system. The dynamical phases are distinguished by a unifying, trajectory- based order parameter, realized as a classical correlation function and a sequential quantum weak value.
summary: This paper presents a unified theory connecting dynamical phase transitions in quantum systems (unitary evolution) and classical systems (dissipative relaxation). By analyzing the complex-time behavior of a dynamical generating function, the authors show that the semiclassical limit bridges the gap, allowing single-particle quantum systems to exhibit transitions analogous to those found in classical statistical mechanics.
main_problem: The paper unifies the description of dynamical phase transitions (DPTs) occurring in both the unitary evolution of an isolated quantum particle and the dissipative relaxation of a classical Brownian particle.
main_result: It establishes a direct, unified connection between quantum and classical finite-time DPTs, showing that the semiclassical limit acts analogously to the thermodynamic limit.
method: The analysis employs a dynamical generating function, utilizing saddle-point approximations of path integrals and analyzing the condensation of Fisher zeros in the complex-time plane.
model_or_system: The models include a quantum particle undergoing quench dynamics and a classical Brownian particle relaxing in a potential, both analyzed via their respective propagators or Fokker-Planck equations.
key_observables: Survival Amplitude (SA)/Survival Rate Function (SRF), and a unifying, trajectory-based order parameter realized as a classical correlation function and a sequential quantum weak value.
important_parameters: Semiclassical limit ($\hbar 	o 0$) and weak-noise limit ($\eta 	o 0$); the competition between different saddle trajectories.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies heavily on the saddle-point approximation for the path integral and the identification of Fisher zeros in the complex time plane.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate saddle trajectories determining the propagator, and show the SRF for both quantum and classical problems, revealing kinks at critical times.
paper_structure: The paper develops the unifying framework by first analyzing the quantum and classical dynamics separately using the generating function, then demonstrating the correspondence through the complex-time structure of the Fisher zeros, and finally defining the shared order parameter.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it provides a powerful, unified mathematical framework to study non-equilibrium dynamics and phase transitions in both quantum and classical regimes, extending concepts from many-body physics to single-particle systems.
